MEET MESA · MEMORY FOR AI

Give your AI a memory it can trace.

MESA is open-source memory infrastructure for AI systems. It stores information from your documents and notes, finds what is relevant to a question, and returns it with the source.

See how it worksExplore the example
THE IDEA IN ONE LINE

Keep the information. Keep where it came from.

WHY A MEMORY LAYER?

Your assistant needs more than a question.

To answer using your own information, an assistant needs relevant material from your documents. MESA keeps that material retrievable beyond a single conversation, together with the passage and document revision that support it.

WHAT HAPPENS TO A NOTE?

Add it once. Find it with its source.

Follow a fictional archive note from input to the evidence your application receives.

A note’s journey through memory
01 / 04

Start with a simple note.

Your application sends this text and its source identity to MESA. Acceptance starts background processing; it does not mean processing is complete.

Source · Atlas visitor guide / revision 1
“The Atlas archive opens at 09:00 on weekdays.”
Information + source identity
02 / 04

The fact stays connected to the note.

MESA extracts structured facts, applies the configured validation and writes the main record. Search representations follow in order. A successful write ends at COMMITTED.

Structured fact → original passage
Atlas archive → weekday opening time → 09:00
Information + source identity
03 / 04

Look for meaning, words and connections.

The application asks a question. MESA searches eligible records using meaning, keywords, structured facts and bounded relationships, then combines their rankings.

Question from your application
“When can I visit the Atlas archive on Monday?”
Information + source identity
04 / 04

The application receives the basis of an answer.

MESA returns relevant information with its document, revision and supporting passage. Your application’s language model can use this context to write an answer.

Evidence returned by MESA
09:00 · Atlas visitor guide · revision 1 · supporting passage
Information + source identity

Illustrative walkthrough, not a live query or measured result. The Atlas note is fictional.

WHAT CAN YOU BUILD?

Put your information to work.

01

An assistant for your documents

Find relevant passages in a collection of notes or documents, and show which source supports the information.

02

Memory across sessions

Let an agent retrieve previously saved information in later sessions, within its authorized data scope.

03

Work that needs source tracing

Build review workflows where a fact must be traced to a specific document revision and passage.

These are possible application patterns, not claims of deployed customer systems.

START WITH THE CORE

Memory is one part of the application.

Core handles memory. Your application supplies source text and uses a language model to turn returned evidence into an answer. HTTP, Python and the V4 MCP gateway provide integration paths.

MESA Data → MESA Core → MESA Law

The legal reference path: source preparation → memory → application. Data and Law are separate projects; Core can also serve other applications.
